messages.subject: mean intensities for each segement
parts:
Hi,

I know how to get the mean sepctrum for each segement after segmentation by for example spatial shrunken centroids. 
But I was wondering if there is an easy way to get a list with the mean instensities for each m/z value for each segment?

Kind regards,

Ellen Borms

messages.author: 23c079b0573006a3
messages.subject: Re: mean intensities for each segement
parts:
Hi, I wrote a little function for getting such values, there are probably better ways and there may be a way already embedded in the package. Trying to contribute after all the great work of Kyle has done anyhow.


require(plyr)
require(reshape2)

## returns data.frame with segment mean, sd,and cv for every mass bin:

segment_stats <- function(cardinaldata,grouping=sscgdata$classes){
  cardinaldata_df <- data.frame(grouping,t(iData(cardinaldata)))
  colnames(cardinaldata_df) <- c("segment",fData(cardinaldata)$mz)
  cardinaldata_df<-na.omit(cardinaldata_df)[1:length(cardinaldata_df)]
  
  melted <- melt(cardinaldata_df,variable.name = "mass")
  analysisoutput<-ddply(melted, c("segment", "mass"), summarise,
                        mean = mean(value), sd = sd(value),
                        cv = sd(value)/mean(value)
  )

  return(analysisoutput) 
}

analysis_df <- segment_stats(mydata, grouping=mysscgdata$classes

##output looks like this:

head(analysis_df)

cardinaldata is the the msset data, will be less computer calc if it is already picked peaks
sscgdata is a spatialShrunkenCentroids analysis. it is listed as:

sscgdata$classes

this assumes you did you not run the sscg with multiple parameters, i.e. k=c(5,10)...etc
if so, you will have to access the classes through a list
sscgdata$classes[[1]]
sscgdata$classes[[2]]

messages.author: 6033d3c0e7d242fa
messages.subject: Re: mean intensities for each segement
parts:
Heath shows the most straightforward way above using featureApply().

Rather than pass multiple functions, you can define a new function that returns everything you want.

myfun <- function(x) c(mean(x),var(x))
df <-featureApply(cardinaldata,.pixel.groups=sscgdata$classes[[1]],.fun=myfun)

If the shrunken centroids from the results are adequate, you could also do something like

df <- topLabels(sscgdata,model=1,sort.by="classes",type="-",n=Inf)
